summary: Authoritative, DNSSEC-signed DNS for infra.test is operational. Node1 is the primary, node2/node3 are secondaries, and node4 persistently uses both secondaries. Authenticated updates, propagation, and single-server failover were behaviorally verified.
actions_performed: Installed and enabled BIND on node1-node3 and DNS utilities on node4.
Published app.infra.test as 10.100.145.10 and status.infra.test as "ready".
Configured automatic ECDSAP256SHA256 DNSSEC signing and verified the final zone cryptographically.
Generated a restricted HMAC-SHA256 update key on node1 and configured TSIG update policy.
Configured node4's persistent NetworkManager profile with node2 and node3 as resolvers.
Tested update propagation and removed the temporary test record afterward.
Stopped and restored node2 while confirming node4 failed over to node3.

evidence.requirement: Primary/secondary authoritative topology and required records
evidence.summary: All services are active and enabled at final serial 2026090106. Direct queries from node1-node3 returned authoritative AA answers for app=10.100.145.10 and status="ready".
The final zone passed dnssec-verify as fully signed with ECDSAP256SHA256; all three authorities served RRSIG records.

evidence.requirement: Authenticated updates from node1 propagated to both secondaries
evidence.summary: An unsigned update was REFUSED; the TSIG-authenticated update advanced the serial and appeared signed on both secondaries. Its cleanup then propagated to both at serial 2026090106.
Node4's persistent and active resolver configuration lists 10.100.145.11 and 10.100.145.12, and direct checks through each returned the required records.

evidence.requirement: Resolution remains available when one authoritative server is unavailable
evidence.summary: Baseline resolution used node2; node2 was stopped and had no port-53 listener; node4 continued resolving signed data through node3; node2 was restored at the current serial and both servers were healthy afterward.
